edges.text: General entry requirements and Physics level 1b or level 1a2, Chemistry level 2, Mathematics Further level 2, or Physics 1a or 1b1+1b2, Chemistry 2, Mathematics 4/Mathematics D
120 credits including 60 credits in chemistry. Admission requires a project plan accepted by the department. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6.
120 credits including 60 credits in chemistry. Admission requires a project plan accepted by the department. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6.

15 credits Chemistry including 5 credits from any of the courses Chemical Principles 10 credits, Basic Chemistry 10 credits, General Chemistry, or The Basic Principles of Chemistry, as well as participation in other Chemistry courses for 15 cr.
60 credits in science/engineering. Participation in Solid State Chemistry or the course can be taken in parallel.
60 credits in science/engineering including Inorganic Chemistry I, 10 credits, or Physical Chemistry, 10 credits, or Basic Materials Chemistry, 5 credits.
120 credits in science/engineering including 20 credits in chemistry. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6.
120 credits and participation in Biomaterials I, 5 credits. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6.
120 credits including Materials Chemistry, 10 credits. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6.

120 credits with 90 credits in chemistry and physics, with at least 60 credits in chemistry. 5 credits electrochemistry. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6.

120 credits in science/engineering. Materials Chemistry 10 credits, and participation in Physics and Chemistry of Surfaces, and Engineering Materials, and Surface Engineering and Materials Selection for Function and Design. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6.

120 credits in science/engineering, including Materials chemistry 10 credits, or Introduction to Materials Science 10 hp, or Introduction to materials engineering 5 credits, or Materials Chemistry 5 hp. Participation in Surface and Materials Analysis 5 credits, or Materials Analysis for Batteries 10 hp, or Material Synthesis and Characterisation 10 hp.
120 credits with 30 credits in chemistry. 5 credits physical chemistry or Materials chemistry, 10 credits. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6.

Alternative 1: 120 credits with 90 credits in chemistry, including Spectroscopy or Photochemistry. Participation in Advanced Electrochemistry. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6. Alternative 2: 120 credits with 75 credits in physics or chemistry, and 30 credits materials science. Participation in Photochemistry. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6. Alternative 3: 120 credits in science/engineering. 5 credits at advanced level. Materials chemistry, Electrochemistry and Quantum mechanics and chemical bonding II. Patricipation in Solid State Physics I. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6.

120 credits in science/engineering with (1) 60 credits in chemistry or (2) 30 credits in chemistry and 30 credits in physics/biology. Participation in Biomaterials I of which 2 credits completed or participation in Materials synthesis of which 2 credits completed. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6.

One of the following is required: (1) 120 credits with 60 credits in chemistry, including 20 credits in biochemistry, or (2) 120 credits with 30 credits in chemistry and 30 credits in biology, including 20 credits in biochemistry, or (3) 120 credits within the Master's Programme in Molecular Biotechnology Engineering, including Cell Biology, 15 credits, or (4) 120 credits within the Master's Programme in Chemical Engineering, including Physiology and Molecular Cell Biology and Development of Biologicals. Also required is 10 credits at Master's level. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6.
60 credits in science/engineering including 10 credits organic chemistry.

120 credits with 60 credits in chemistry including Organic Chemistry I, 10 credits, or Physical Chemistry, 10 credits, or the equivalent. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6.

120 credits with 5 credits at Master's level. Participation in NMR Spectroscopy I or participation in Spectroscopic Methods for Organic Chemistry. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6.

120 credits with 60 credits in chemistry including 15 credits in organic chemistry. 5 credits at Master's level. Participation in Organic Chemistry III or Organic Reaction Principles. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6.
Participation in Quantum Mechanics and Chemical Bonding I or Theoretical Chemistry 10 credits.

120 credits with 100 credits in science/engineering including 15 credits in mathematics and 75 credits in physics, chemistry, materials science and/or materials engineering, and one of the following: 1) Quantum Mechanics and Chemical Bonding I and any of the courses Solid State Physics, 5 credits, and Solid State Chemistry, 5 credits; 2) 30 credits in materials science; 3) Participation in Introduction to Energy storage and Materials for Batteries. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6.

120 credits in science/engineering including 15 credits in mathematics, and Computer Programming I, or Introduction to energy storage, or Introduction to Materials Science 10 credits. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6.

120 credits in science/engineering including 30 credits in chemistry and/or chemical engineering. Either (1) Participation in both Introduction to Energy Storage and Materials Chemistry for Batteries or (2) Materials Chemistry 10 credits and participation in Materials and Manufacturing Processes I. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6.
At least 120 credits within science and/or engineering. Participation in Electrochemistry for batteries II. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6.
120 credits in science/engineering. Participation in Rechargeable batteries 10 credits. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6.

120 credits with 60 credits in chemistry including 10 credits in organic chemistry and 10 credits in physical chemistry. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6.

Participation in one of the courses Basic Course in Mathematics, Basic Algebra, Algebra and Vector Geometry, Basic Algebra or Algebra and Geometry. The course can be taken in parallel with one of these courses.
Participation in Single Variable Calculus or Calculus in One Variable. Participation in Linear Algebra I or Algebra and Geometry.
Participation in Basic Course in Mathematics or Basic Algebra.
Participation in Algebra and Geometry, Basic Course in Mathematics or Basic Algebra. Participation in Single Variable Calculus which may also be taken in parallel with this course.

Participation in a course in programming in Python (for example Computer Programming I), or the course can be taken in parallel. Participation in one of the courses Single Variable Calculus, Single Variable Calculus M, Geometry and Calculus and Calculus for Engineers.
General entry requirements and Mathematics Further level 1c, or Mathematics 3c/Mathematics D

120 credits in science/engineering. One of these alternatives: 1) Solid state physics F and attended course in Semiconductor Electronics, 2) Materials chemistry and attended course in Solid state physics I, 3) Introduction to materials engineering or Introduction to material science (10 credits). Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6.

130 credits in science/engineering. Either materials chemistry and attended course in Surface physics and chemistry or Surface physics. Attended course in surface characterisation or Surface and materials analysis. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6.
130 credits in science/engineering. Micro- and Nanotechnology I should have been attended. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6.
120 credits in science/engineering including Micro and nanotechnology I. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6.

120 credits in science/engineering. Either: Solid State Physics I, Surface Characterisation and Surface and Materials Analysis; or: Introduction to Materials Engineering, Surface Characterisation and participation in Materials Analysis. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6.
60 credits within Science/Technology. Participation in Quantum Mechanics and Chemical Bonding II and either Thermodynamics, Chemical Thermodynamics or Principles of Thermodynamics.
130 credits in science/engineering. Engineering Materials. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6.
130 credits in science/engineering. Tribological Materials. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6.
120 credits in science/engineering. Micro- and Nanotechnology I must have been taken. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6.
120 credits in science/engineering including either Introduction to Additive Manufacturing or Materials Chemistry. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6.

120 credits in science/engineering including either (1) Polymer Technology, (2) Polymer materials or (3) Polymer Chemistry and Engineering Materials. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6.
120 credits in science/engineering. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6. (A Swedish Bachelor's degree fulfils the requirement in English.)
120 credits in science/engineering. Biomaterials I or Bio-MEMS and organs-on-chip. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6.

120 credits in science/engineering. At least 3 credits from Materials Chemistry or at least 2 credits from Introduction to Materials Engineering. Surface Characterisation must have been taken. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6.

150 credits, including 90 credits in biomedicine, pharmaceutical science, chemistry, natural science and/or engineering. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6.

150 credits of which 120 credits biomedicine, biology, pharmaceutical sciences, chemistry and/or science/technology. Earlier studies should contain 7.5 credits pharmacology. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6.

150 credits in biomedicine, pharmaceutical science, drug development, natural science and/or technology. Previous studies must contain 5 credits of statistics or probability theory. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6.

150 credits, including 120 credits in biomedicine, biology, pharmaceutical sciences, chemistry and/or natural sciences/technology. Previous studies should include 5 credits of pharmacokinetics and 7.5 credits of pharmacology. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6.
150 credits in biomedicine, pharmaceutical science, chemistry, drug development, natural science and/or technology. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6.

150 credits including knowledge corresponding to at least 60 credits in the subjects chemistry, biology, biochemistry, pharmaceutical science or medicine. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6.
150 credits, including 120 credits in biomedicine, pharmaceutical science, chemistry, pharmaceutical development, natural science and/or technology and 4 credits in Bioinformatics.
150 credits in chemistry, biology, biochemistry, pharmacy, medicine or dentistry; or other equivalent education under special review.

120 credits in biomedicine, pharmaceutical science, natural sciences and/or engineering. Prior studies must include 15 credits general and organic chemistry, 6 credits physiology and 7.5 credits pharmacology.
Biochemistry I
150 credits, including 120 credits in biomedicine, pharmaceutical science, chemistry, pharmaceutical development, natural science and/or engineering.

150 credits, including 120 credits in biomedicine, pharmaceutical science, chemistry, drug discovery, natural science and/or engineering. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6.

150 credits, including 120 credits in biomedicine, pharmaceutical sciences, drug development and/or natural sciences/engineering. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6.
Participation in Pharmaceutics

150 credits, including 120 credits in biomedicine, pharmaceutical sciences and/or natural sciences/engineering. Previous studies must include 3 credits of pharmaceutics and pharmacokinetics. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6.

180 credits including Analytical Chemistry with Data Analysis and Chemometrics. Participation in Pharmaceutics with 2.5 credits passed, and in Spectroscopic Methods for Organic Chemistry with 3 credits passed.

150 credits of which 120 credits in biomedicine, pharmaceutical science, natural science and/or technology. Prior studies should include 10 credits in general chemistry and organic chemistry. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6.

150 credits of which 90 credits in biomedicine, pharmaceutical science, natural science and/or technology. Prior studies should include 10 credits in chemistry and 7.5 credits in pharmacology. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6.

150 credits of which 120 credits in biomedicine, pharmaceutical science, natural science and/or technology. Prior studies should include 10 credits in general chemistry and organic chemistry. Participation in the course Computational Medicinal Chemistry. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6.

150 credits, including 60 credits in chemistry or biology and advanced courses (at level G2F/C or above) in pharmaceutical sciences worth at least 22.5 credits or Pharmacognosy B (15 credits). Alternatively, from the Master of Science Programme in Pharmacy: 150 credits in the programme including a course in pharmacognosy; or from the Master's Programme in Chemical Engineering: 150 credits in the programme including courses in analytical chemistry (10 credits), pharmacology (7.5 credits) and medicinal chemistry (7.5 credits); or admission to the Master's Programme in Drug Discovery and Development. Proficiency in English equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course English 6.
